title: Technical Specifications Bias
learning_objectives: Convert brand-like requirements to functional requirements
Document market availability to ensure competition
red_flags: Specs mirroring a specific vendor brochure
Extremely narrow dimensions or proprietary features

n1.text: A technical department submits specifications that read identically to a specific product brochure.

A.text: Request the department to rewrite the specs focusing on functional requirements and equivalent standards.
A.feedback: Correct. Functional requirements ensure broad competition and better value.
A.expert_log: Required rewrite of specs to functional requirements.

B.text: Publish the specs as-is to save time and meet the department request.
B.feedback: Publishing biased specs severely restricts competition and increases audit risk.

C.text: Add an "or equivalent" clause at the end of the document without changing the specific metrics.
C.feedback: Adding "or equivalent" is insufficient if the core metrics still practically exclude all other vendors.
C.expert_log: Used weak mitigation (or equivalent clause) on highly restrictive specs.

n2.text: The department argues the functional specs might allow inferior products to win.
n2.challenge: How do you ensure quality without restricting competition?

A.text: Implement objective performance criteria and quality thresholds in the evaluation phase.
A.feedback: Excellent. Objective performance criteria protect quality while maintaining open competition.

B.text: Revert to the original brand-specific specs to ensure quality.
B.feedback: Reverting to biased specs weakens the audit defensibility of the tender.
B.expert_log: Reverted to restrictive specifications under departmental pressure, increasing audit risk.

C.text: Require bidders to provide samples of the specific brand.
C.feedback: Requiring a specific brand sample may severely restrict competition and requires further procurement review.
C.expert_log: Required specific brand samples, raising severe audit concerns.

n3.text: During the tender, multiple suppliers complain that the specs are tailored to one vendor.
n3.challenge: How do you handle the complaints?

A.text: Suspend the tender, review the specs, and issue a corrigendum broadening the requirements.
A.feedback: Corrective action mitigates the risk, though it costs time.
A.expert_log: Suspended tender and issued corrigendum to fix bias.

B.text: Ignore the complaints as they come from competitors.
B.feedback: Ignoring valid market complaints invites formal appeals and severe audit findings.
B.expert_log: Ignored valid supplier complaints about restrictive specs.

C.text: Cancel the tender entirely and use a direct award due to urgency.
C.feedback: Using urgency to bypass a flawed specification process creates a significant audit concern and requires further review.
C.expert_log: Improperly converted tender to urgent direct award, creating weak evidence trail.
